newsitem.title: USA: US WEST COAST CRUDES FALL, ALASKAN CRUDE SELLS.
newsitem.headline: US WEST COAST CRUDES FALL, ALASKAN CRUDE SELLS.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices tracked broader market losses Friday while discounts for local benchmark grade Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude stayed flat, traders said.
Spot trade was razor thin in typically quiet Friday market.
On Thursday, a West Coast refiner sold ANS crude at $1.97 a barrel under September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) crude for delivery next month, traders said.
The refiner, which typically buys ANS, sold the cargo because it replaced its ANS supply with Colombian South Blend, traders said.
The discount has shrunk since a mid-June cargo sold at minus $2.08, then held there for over a month after refiners saw weak gasoline prices diminish their buying power.
But with margins over $10.00 a barrel now, traders are looking to buy more ANS, and the grade's main seller, BP Oil, has stepped out of the market to evaluate its pricing.
Meanwhile, Friday's spot price for WTI dropped 55 cents a barrel to $19.54 as traders expected supplies to increase when Iraqi resumed oil exports in the coming days, traders said.
Wilmington grades fell with lower postings on Friday.
